The Faculty of Associated Medical Sciences at Chiang Mai University, along with the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development, has been involved in service integration and programmatic linkages for key populations in Ukraine and the European Region. 2. In Thailand, within the SEA Region, efforts have been made to integrate services for the general population, focusing on increasing HIV testing uptake among tuberculosis clients. This initiative, implemented in Indonesia within the Western Pacific Region, targets people with TB through service integration and programmatic linkages. 3. In Myanmar, organizations such as Medical Action Myanmar, the National AIDS Program, and the Myanmar Oxford Clinical Research Unit have implemented integrated community-based harm reduction programs. These programs aim to improve access and linkages to treatment and care for people who inject drugs and the general population. 4. In India, PATH has worked on strengthening public-private sector integration to accelerate HIV case-finding and linkage to treatment among people with TB. This initiative is part of the SEA Region's efforts to enhance service integration and programmatic linkages. 5. In Kenya, PATH has developed integrative care approaches targeting men by using hypertension services as an entry point for HIV testing services (HTS). This program focuses on men and the general population within the African Region. 6. In Vietnam, PATH has introduced innovative community-based HIV testing services tailored for men who have sex with men, transgender individuals, and other key populations. These services aim to improve linkage to care and treatment within the Western Pacific Region. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) has supported community-led testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C virus (HCV) in Vietnam. This initiative targets people who inject drugs, men who have sex with men, sex workers, and their partners, emphasizing service integration and programmatic linkages. 8. In Mozambique, Jhpiego has implemented community HIV counseling and testing programs using strategic information tools. These programs target the general population within the African Region. 9. PATH has utilized user personas to design and deliver new HIV self-testing services in South Africa and Vietnam. These efforts focus on the general population and key populations within the African and Western Pacific Regions. 10. In India, the National AIDS Control Organization has used program data to prioritize HIV testing scale-up and optimize yield. This initiative targets the general population and key populations within the SEA Region. 11. The WHO issued a call for case examples and good practices in HIV testing services on March 20, 2019. This call aimed to gather evidence to update the Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Testing Services, focusing on optimizing newer service delivery approaches, demand creation strategies, and simplified testing strategies. 12. HIV testing services encompass a comprehensive range of activities, including pre-test and post-test counseling, linkage to prevention, treatment, and care services, and coordination with laboratory services to ensure quality assurance and accurate results. 13. All HIV testing services must adhere to WHO's essential 5 Cs: Consent, Confidentiality, Counseling, Correct test results, and Connection to prevention, care, and treatment. 14. Successful case studies of HIV testing services may be included in the upcoming Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Testing Services, planned for release in December 2018. These case studies should be concise, evidence-based, and include relevant data and photographs. 15. The WHO seeks case examples that describe HIV testing programs with themes such as service integration, partner notification services, demand creation, risk-based screening tools, and multiplex testing, particularly HIV/syphilis dual tests. 16. Case examples should be approximately 400 words long and address specific subheadings, including program aims, methodologies, measures of success, and challenges or failures. 17. The WHO has developed a scoring tool to evaluate case examples based on their quality, relevance, and potential to inform future programming. Strong case examples should clearly describe program settings, methods, data, and evidence of success or challenges. 18. Selected case examples may be published in the main body of the guidelines or included in an annex, depending on their content and relevance.
